title: Design System: New Orleans Complete Streets Coalition

display.purpose: Condensed bold homepage headline; explicit local-brand typography exception.

page-title.purpose: Reading-page introduction with its own responsive title scale.

headline.purpose: Major editorial sections; prose uses smaller explicit overrides.

title.purpose: Campaign and related record headings; resource and directory variants enlarge the base.

body.purpose: Long-form reading and explanations; 18px on phones, constrained to 69ch in articles.

lead.purpose: Short introductory paragraphs; homepage and phone values are contextual overrides.

label.purpose: Real dates, publishers, source notes and update context; not decorative eyebrows.

navigation.purpose: Semibold navigation and compact primary buttons.

button.purpose: Standard primary, outline and invitation actions.

text-link.purpose: Semibold underlined action with an inline arrow.

shadows.name: navigation-panel
shadows.purpose: Desktop dropdown separation only; removed when the navigation panel enters mobile document flow.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: Shared ease-out curve for button state and image-hover transitions.

motion.name: m-ease-enter
motion.purpose: Hero photograph settling and existing photo-chapter transitions.

motion.name: m-image
motion.purpose: Campaign photograph hover zoom to 1.03 inside its frame.

motion.name: m-image-out
motion.purpose: Campaign photograph settling back from hover.

motion.name: hero-image-settle
motion.purpose: Photograph scale and clip settling during the one hero entrance.

narrative.overview:
The coalition's original identity is the visual authority: its supplied logo, strong blue headings, yellow actions and grey dividers carry through a bright public website. Locally hosted Barlow Condensed gives headlines the sturdy character of the mark; full-width Barlow gives explanations, policies and evidence room to be read. This pairing is an explicit original-brand exception to generic font restrictions, not a license to substitute a different display face.

Real photographs from coalition materials establish place and show different ways of moving. The interface uses open editorial sections, plain language and visible source information. Short invitation pages can be spacious; policy, research and archive pages follow their content's natural height. The shared system is the palette, typography, alignment, imagery and interaction behavior; the homepage's particular sequence is recorded separately in its surface brief.

Documentation basis: the implemented Astro components, pages, global stylesheet and loaded motion assets. This is a code scan, not visual signoff. Browser captures and computed-style sampling were unavailable because the sandbox rejected localhost listeners with `EPERM`; responsive appearance and final visual quality still require browser verification.
keyCharacteristics: Original coalition blue, yellow and grey on white and warm paper.
Bold condensed headlines with readable full-width body text.
Actual community photography with a clear connection to the content.
Open rows, restrained dividers and content-led reading layouts.
Visible keyboard focus, native disclosure controls and reduced-motion fallbacks.

rules.name: The Original Identity Rule
rules.body: Keep the coalition's supplied logo and blue, yellow and grey identity; derive new surfaces from their existing roles.

rules.name: The Brand Type Rule
rules.body: Use the supplied local Barlow families and their actual weights; preserve this explicit brand decision on future surfaces.

rules.name: The Reading Length Rule
rules.body: Let policy, research and archive pages grow with their content; keep paragraphs, source lists and tables within readable measures.

rules.name: The Open Surface Rule
rules.body: Use alignment, spacing and dividers for editorial records; reserve elevated panels for controls that actually overlap the page.

dos: **Do** preserve the supplied logo, original palette and local Barlow font pairing.
**Do** use real coalition photographs and identify a design concept as a concept.
**Do** keep body copy readable, record titles clear and source context close to the claim.
**Do** let reading pages follow their content's natural height.
**Do** use visible focus, native disclosure controls and explicit external links for embedded maps.
**Do** retain reduced-motion and no-script access to the complete content.
donts: **Don't** replace the approved brand typography with a generic display or system-font identity.
**Don't** introduce decorative pre-heading labels, invented statistics or unsupported claims.
**Don't** put long reading copy directly over a busy photograph; use a solid surface for image notes.
**Don't** turn editorial lists and report measures into floating card grids.
**Don't** make a surface's particular narrative sequence a mandatory template for every page.
**Don't** describe code inspection as completed browser or visual verification.
